demand.reason: Global natural graphite mine production is estimated at ~1.63 million metric tons annually, placing it securely within the highest absolute demand band of >1,000,000 tons.

growth.reason: Demand is projected for rapid growth exceeding 12% CAGR. Driven by EV battery gigafactories requiring 50–100 kg of spherical graphite per vehicle anode, independent trackers forecast a >140% consumption expansion through 2030.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: Extraction concentration is high. China produced 1.4 of the 1.8 million tons mined in 2025 (78%), followed by Madagascar (4%), placing primary mining diversity in the 65–85% band (Score 4). 


Refining: Downstream spheronization and chemical purification to 99.95% C for battery anodes is heavily concentrated in China, which dictates over 90% of global processing capacity, exceeding the 85% threshold (Score 5).

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: Global reserves are abundant, estimated at 310 million tons. Measured against current extraction rates, known economic resources represent over 170 years of supply, which is effectively limitless (>100 years). 


Diversification: Known reserve structures are well-distributed. China holds 32% and Brazil holds 24% of the global reserve base, maintaining a balanced HHI index between 0.15–0.25 (Score 2).

end_use.reason:
Defense & National Security (+1.5): carbon-carbon graphite composites are critical for military rocket nozzles, missile nose cones, and aerospace brake arrays. Energy Generation & Grid (+1.5): functions as the dominant anode material in utility lithium-ion batteries and as nuclear reactor moderators. Advanced Semiconductors & Computing (+1.0): utilized widely across semiconductor tool components and high-performance graphene hardware. Electrification & Transport (+1.0): indispensable for electric vehicle battery anode configurations. Construction & Heavy Industry (+0.5): graphite electrodes serve as primary bulk inputs for electric arc furnace steelmaking refractories. 


Sector presence scores total 5.5 across 5 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus adds +2.0, yielding an objective composite score of 7.5.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Synthetic graphite from petroleum coke acts as a commercially deployed battery substitute, and silicon anodes are emerging, but they introduce higher production costs and performance trade-offs, matching Score 3. 


Recyclability: Recractory steelmaking recycling is active, but commercial battery-grade recovery from end-of-life EV batteries is not yet deployed at scale due to low residual value, tracking in the negligible recycling tier (<5%).

extraction_refining.reason: Flotation concentration is standard, but downstream chemical refining into battery-grade spherical shapes requires high-temperature graphitization at 3000°C or intense hydrofluoric acid treatments. The environmental management requirements present a complex and specialized barrier.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline is adequate. Driven by EV battery localization policies, a healthy wave of integrated mine-to-anode builds is under advanced development across Tanzania, Mozambique, and Canada, capable of adding 10–20% to supply within 3–5 years.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: India mined about 17,000 tons in 2025, seventh globally (USGS), but internal capacity falls short of its 150,000-ton battery node targets, leaving the nation ~42% dependent on Chinese imports, matching a significant domestic feedstock base but majority refined import picture. 


Strategic Posture: Graphite is on India's critical list with customs duties reduced. While domestic mining block auctions are active and Coal India is entering the extraction market, India has large synthetic-graphite electrode makers and battery-anode plants under construction (TACC, Epsilon), and although there are no overseas assets, the anode plants put concrete plans in motion (Score 2).

price_volatility.reason: Flake and amorphous commodity pricing followed highly gradual trends, fluctuating safely within a predictable 20–50% multi-year band without sudden exchange-driven price spikes or market breakdown.

capability.name: Graphite
capability.next_move: Synthetic graphite anode for non-China cell makers; secure premium coke.
capability.what_india_has: Large electrode makers with graphitisation know-how (HEG 100 kt, Graphite India 80 kt); TACC's 20 kt/yr anode plant near Indore; Epsilon's planned 100 kt/yr at Bellary; GFCL is setting up an anode facility.
capability.cost: ~US$11-13k per t/yr: Epsilon US$650 m for 50 kt (US) and US$1.1 bn for 100 kt (India) (#9).

strategyList.name: Graphite anode material
strategyList.what: Synthetic: coke graphitised at ~3,000 C. Natural: flake spheroidised and purified. Both are coated.
strategyList.outside_china: China over 90% of anode material; Korea and Indonesia smaller (US anode imports in 2025: China 55%, Indonesia 31%, Korea 14%).
strategyList.cost: Epsilon: US$650 m for 50 kt/yr (North Carolina); US$1.1 bn for 100 kt/yr (Bellary, India).
strategyList.india_base: HEG and Graphite India (graphitisation); TACC (20 kt/yr, Indore); Epsilon; GFCL anode facility.
strategyList.gap: Coke precursors; low-cost power; customer qualification.

strategyList.name: Recycling (batteries, magnets, catalysts, PV)
strategyList.what: Shredding and hydrometallurgy of black mass; magnet recovery; spent-catalyst leaching; PV-panel recovery.
strategyList.outside_china: Battery recycling: China has over three-quarters of pre-treatment and 90% of material-recovery capacity; Europe, Japan, Korea and the US smaller.
strategyList.cost: India's scheme expects ~Rs 8,000 crore for 270+ kt/yr of capacity (~Rs 30 crore per kt/yr), yielding ~40 kt/yr of critical minerals.
strategyList.india_base: Lohum, Rubamin, the Bhopal magnet facility, CSIR-NML; Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme (2025).

chemistryList.name: Fluorochemicals and HF
chemistryList.who: GFCL (India's largest integrated fluoropolymer maker; fluorspar mine in Morocco); Navin Fluorine (AHF project at Dahej).
chemistryList.carries_over_to: LiPF6 electrolyte salt; HF purification of graphite; rare-earth fluorides for metal making; etching chemicals for gallium and silicon devices.
chemistryList.fit: Direct for LiPF6; adjacent for the rest
chemistryList.summary: Fluorine chemistry is a shared industrial foundation for battery salts, selected mineral-purification routes and electronic chemicals. India's existing HF plants provide a starting point, but each application needs its own process, purity controls and customer qualification.

links.how: HF can remove silicate impurities from natural graphite. KIGAM-led experiments on one Korean ore found large purity improvements with HF, but this is feed-specific laboratory evidence, not a performance guarantee for Indian ores or a qualified anode product.

chemistryList.name: Carbon and graphitisation
chemistryList.who: HEG and Graphite India (electrodes); TACC; Epsilon.
chemistryList.summary: India's electrode industry supplies furnace engineering and carbon-processing experience. Battery anodes require a separate product chain: controlled powders, purification, coatings and qualification in customers' cells. Silicon–carbon composites are another extension, with additional materials and performance requirements.

links.how: Adds the conversion steps between carbon feedstock or flake concentrate and anode active material. This is where carbon-processing capability can serve domestic cell production rather than only metallurgical applications.
links.fit: Direct processing opportunity; customer qualification required
